title: Effect of a cod protein hydrolysate on postprandial glucose metabolism in healthy subjects: a double-blind cross-over trial

what_it_measured.text: The primary outcome was postprandial response in glucose metabolism, measured by samples of serum glucose, insulin and plasma glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) in 20 min intervals for 180 min.

The aim of the present study was to assess the effect of a marine protein hydrolysate (MPH) from Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) on postprandial glucose metabolism in healthy, middle-aged to elderly subjects.

dose.text: The intervention implemented 20 mg of MPH per kg body weight (test material) or control (casein).

route.text: MPH or casein powder (identical, both ﬂavoured with lemon) was mixed with water and taken before a standardised breakfast meal, in randomised order.

endpoint.text: The primary outcome was postprandial response in glucose metabolism, measured by samples of serum glucose, insulin and plasma glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) in 20 min intervals for 180 min.
The secondary outcome was adverse events measured by symptom questionnaires.

reported_results.text: The postprandial insulin concentration was signiﬁcantly lower after MPH compared with control (mean difference between geometric means: 1·067 (95 % CI 1·01, 1·13) mIU/l; P = 0·032).

In a mixed-model regression analysis, no differences were observed between MPH and control for postprandial glucose concentration (mean difference: −0·04 (95 % CI –0·17, 0·09) mmol/l; P = 0·573) or GLP-1 concentration (mean difference between geometric means: 1·02 (95 % CI 0·99, 1·06) pmol/l; P = 0·250).

In a multivariable, repeated-measures linear mixed-effects regression analysis, no differences were observed between MPH and control for glucose concentration (mean difference: −0·04 (95 % CI –0·17, 0·09) mmol/l; P = 0·573).
The AUC for the glucose concentration was numerically equal between MPH (1078 (95 % CI 956·0, 1199·0) mmol/l × min) and control (1068 (95 % CI 944·8, 1190·0) mmol/l × min; P = 0·910).
(Cmax) occurred 20 min after the meal for both MPH and control and was numerically higher after MPH than after the control drink (7·6 (SD 1·8) v. 7·4 (SD 1·5) mmol/l, respectively; P = 0·997).
No differences were observed between MPH and control for GLP-1 concentration (mean difference between geometric means: 1·02 (95 % CI 0·99, 1·06) pmol/l; P = 0·250).
